newsitem.title: LATVIA: Kaija dominates Latvia shares, Shipyard debuts.
newsitem.headline: Kaija dominates Latvia shares, Shipyard debuts.

text.p: Fish cannery Kaija dominated a quiet share market on Monday as its price rose ahead of its move to the official list from the secondary market and attention was also on Riga Shipyard as it debuted, dealers said.
Total share volume was just under 50,000 lats compared with 46,000 lats on Friday.
Kaija was most traded at 12,900 lats and added 14.7 percent to 2.58 lats.
Riga Shipyard began its life on the stock exchange official list with an opening quote of 1.43 lats verus a privatisation price of 1.39 lats at auction in early April.
"It looks like that is more or less a good price," said one trader, noting that the company announced losses for the first quarter of 1997.
The gains in Kaija helped the Rietumu Bank index to rise by 0.16 percent to 176.5.
Dealers said the market was fairly optimistic about Kaija.
The company has announced an audited 1996 net profit of 639,893 lats against a loss of 200,615 lats in 1995 and that it expected a 1997 profit of 1.1 million lats.
Daugavpils Chain slipped today as the market prepares for the arrival of new shares on the market.
The company has said it wants to issue 84 new shares for every 100 held. Its shares fell by 1.7 percent to 2.36 lats.
Other shares on the official list showed moderate activity.

Unibanka turned over 4,600 lats and added one santime to 3.50 lats, Staburadze traded 3,700 lats to be stable at 2.65 lats while Riga Transport Fleet saw activity of 3,600 lats and lost one santime to 1.23 lats.
